title: File errors, safe closing, buffering and portable text/binary modes (CodeSaathi extension)
learningObjectives: Check errors returned by write, flush and close operations.
Explain how buffered output can delay detection of write failures.
Use fflush and fclose appropriately and check their results.
Distinguish text and binary stream modes where implementations treat them differently.
Ensure each opened stream is closed exactly once on all control-flow paths.

understand.concept: C streams may buffer output. Errors can occur during writes, flushes or close. fflush requests buffered output be delivered to the host environment; fclose closes the stream and can report delayed errors. Text and binary modes may differ on some systems. Resource cleanup must happen on every path after a successful fopen.
understand.whyItMatters: Reliable file handling checks both the operation that writes data and the operation that finalizes the stream. Portable programs must choose text or binary mode intentionally.
understand.analogy: Treat each object or stream as a resource with a defined lifetime and explicit rules for access.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy does not replace C's formal object, storage-duration, alignment or library rules.

explain.narrative:
## 1. Buffered output

The C library may store output temporarily in a stream buffer. A successful fprintf or fputs call does not always mean that the data has reached the host environment.

## 2. Flush explicitly when needed

fflush on an output stream requests delivery of buffered data. It returns EOF if a write error occurs. Do not use fflush on an input stream as a general way to discard unread input; its behavior is not a portable input-buffer clearing technique.

## 3. Close the stream

fclose flushes buffered output and closes the stream. It can report a delayed write error. After fclose, the stream must not be used again, even if fclose reports failure.

## 4. Text and binary modes

Text streams may translate external representations on some implementations. Binary mode is intended for byte-oriented data. Portable programs should not assume that text and binary representations are identical on every platform.

## 5. Reliable cleanup

After fopen succeeds, ensure fclose is reached on every control-flow path. Close exactly once, check its result and report a failed save rather than silently claiming success.

practise.independentTask: Extend CL7.12 with a realistic failure or boundary case. Ensure cleanup is correct, explain the C rule involved, and test both success and failure paths.
hints: Check every relevant library return value.
Keep ownership and cleanup responsibilities explicit.
Do not use a stream after fclose.
Do not assume raw object or file representations are portable.
Test both normal and failure paths.

questions.prompt: When can buffered output errors become visible?
options: During a later flush or close
questions.answer: During a later flush or close
questions.explanation: Buffered data may not be delivered until a flush or close.

questions.prompt: What does fflush do for an output stream?
options: Requests that buffered output be delivered to the host environment
questions.answer: Requests that buffered output be delivered to the host environment
questions.explanation: fflush flushes buffered output and can report an error.

questions.prompt: What should a program do if fclose returns EOF?
options: Treat the close or final output operation as failed
Call fclose repeatedly on the same stream
questions.answer: Treat the close or final output operation as failed
questions.explanation: fclose can report delayed write errors and the stream is no longer usable.

questions.prompt: How many times should a successfully opened stream be closed?
questions.explanation: Every successful open requires one close, with cleanup on all paths.

questions.prompt: Why might text and binary modes behave differently?
options: Some implementations translate text stream representations
questions.answer: Some implementations translate text stream representations
questions.explanation: The C implementation may distinguish text and binary streams.
